result:
I've written the audit to `audit.md`. Summary of verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**, driven by two High findings:

1. **Case-sensitive protected-path list** in `block-destructive-bash.sh:856-857` — the new hidden-directory allowlist relies on case-sensitive matching against `.claude`/`.git`/`.ssh`/etc., so on any case-insensitive filesystem (default macOS, NTFS/WSL) a case-varied path like `./.Claude/` bypasses the block entirely, whereas pre-PR *all* dotfiles were blocked regardless of spelling.
2. **`find_local_source()` in `constructs-lib.sh`** dropped its slug-verification step, so it now returns the first directory in `local_source_paths` that merely looks like a construct — enabling silent substitution of the wrong (or attacker-controlled) local construct for any requested slug.

Plus one Medium (the new protected-dotfile list omits `.netrc`/`.npmrc`/`.git-credentials`/`.pgpass`, which were incidentally protected before this PR). The `symlink-manifest.sh` traversal-check simplification was reviewed and found safe — no action needed there.
